headline: Lights to flag: Verstappen controls every lap in Marina Bay
standfirst: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix for Red Bull Racing, finishing 7.335s ahead of Charles Leclerc, with Kimi Antonelli completing the podium after 62 laps of Singapore.

sections.title: The start
sections.body: Max Verstappen lined up first on the grid. Verstappen converted that into the lead at the end of lap one. The biggest winner of the opening lap was Sainz, up 3 places to 10th.

sections.title: How it unfolded
sections.body: Verstappen was never headed, leading all 62 laps. The race ran green from start to finish.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Verstappen made 1 stop, running soft → medium tyres. The field made 25 pit stops in total; the quickest stationary time was 2.1s for Stroll on lap 26. 7 of the top 10 finishers got home with one stop or fewer.

sections.title: Movers
sections.body: Isack Hadjar made up the most ground, climbing 12 places from 22nd to 10th. Lindblad went the other way, slipping from 9th to 15th. Timing recorded 191 on-track position changes, 19 of them by Hadjar.

sections.title: Retirements
sections.body: Albon (lap 60), Bortoleto (lap 8), Stroll (lap 37) and Colapinto (lap 30) failed to finish.

sections.title: Conditions and pace
sections.body: It stayed dry throughout. Track temperature ranged from 41°C to 44°C, with air at 30–31°C. Charles Leclerc set the fastest lap, a 1:35.202 on lap 41.
